title: Harmonize weight transport API and tokenizer contracts to reduce load-time spikes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: The current model ingest path has grown organically: multiple weight transport formats, inconsistent shard manifest interpretations, and a tokenizer handshake implemented in three places. This causes intermittent load-time memory spikes, duplicate tokenizers for the same model, and brittle fallbacks when format variants are seen in the wild.

Goal: Produce a pragmatic compatibility layer and a single lightweight tokenizer handshake API so that ingestion paths share a single transport contract, eliminate duplicated tokenizer initialization, and enable streaming + lazy activation without regressions for older checkpoint formats. Keep runtime impact minimal and provide a migration shim for existing artifacts.

Scope:
- Define the minimal weight-transport contract (manifest keys, shard ranges, checksum hints) and implement a small canonical parser used by all loaders.
- Replace ad-hoc tokenizer probes with a single TokenizerAdapter API that exposes a deterministic fingerprint and lazy init hooks.
- Implement a migration shim that interprets legacy manifests and emits the canonical manifest at ingest time.
- Optimize the activation path to avoid allocating full tensors for shards until first user request (streaming activation).
- Add unit + integration tests to cover old formats, multishard models, and concurrent ingest scenarios.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of checkpoint formats, changes to on-disk compression formats, or forcing customers to re-export models immediately.
acceptance_criteria: All model loaders import the canonical manifest parser and pass the same manifest test vectors
Single TokenizerAdapter replaces two in-repo ad-hoc impls and is used by runtime and ingest services
Load-time tail latency (99.9th) for model startup reduced by >= 30% on benchmark for 8B and 13B models
No regressions for existing supported checkpoint formats (compatibility tests pass)
Migration shim documented with step-by-step guide and a small CLI tool to rewrite manifests
rollout_plan: 1) Merge canonical manifest parser behind feature flag; 2) Gradually enable ingestion shim for non-production test buckets; 3) Replace tokenizer probes in runtime service and run canary models for 48h; 4) Monitor startup p99, memory peaks, and error rates; 5) Flip feature flag and remove legacy code after 2 successful cycles.
updates: 2025-01-14 - Spike: ran ingest benchmarks across 8B/13B with current pipeline. Observed two classes of startup spikes: tokenizer duplication and eager shard deserialization. Collected heap profiles and sample manifests. (see attachment)

2025-01-20 - Design review with Runtime and Ingest teams. Agreed on a minimal manifest schema (versioned) and that tokenizer should expose a fingerprint + lazy_init(). Action: Asha to write canonical parser draft, Miguel to prototype TokenizerAdapter interface.

2025-01-25 - Prototype: TokenizerAdapter v0 implemented in runtime-service (PR #3128). It provides fingerprint + lazy_init and reduces duplicate tokenizer allocation in the single-host case. Initial tests show ~18% reduced allocation at cold-start.

2025-01-28 - Integration: Migration shim prototype converts legacy manifest variants to canonical format during ingest; CLI available at tools/manifest-rewrite. Ran against internal model bundle corpus (42 models) — 0 conversion failures.

2025-01-30 - Code review feedback on PR #3241: please add concurrency tests for simultaneous ingest + lookup and document API guarantees for TokenizerAdapter under signal handling. Assigned to Miguel for follow-up.
2025-02-04 - Benchmarks: end-to-end p99 startup improvements measured: 35% for 8B (g4dn-like runner), 31% for 13B. Memory peak during ingest reduced by ~22%. Moving to canary rollout next week.
